annotations.text:
Rebuilt to TRICKS_WORK_ORDER.md (design/Tricks.dc.html carries the verdicts).
The counting block is PAPER — card ground, 3px ink, the keypad's bevel at 22px. Tricks is the notebook, not the inventory: its blocks are drawn, not mined. Removal is ABSENCE, not slate: fill drops out, border goes divider, opacity .35 — slate stays reserved for "not yet" on the card screens.
Constant 22px blocks at every n; arrangements may reflow (Fives goes two-column above three ten-frames), the unit never resizes.

Plays ONCE on arrival, then holds the finished state — about 3s to a held result (build 900 staggered · hold 600 · transform 300 · hold 900 · result 300). Again › replays; tapping a chip replays with that number. Under reduced motion the held result renders immediately with the ledger fully lit.
Green only where she acted: the selected chip is deck select's outline treatment (outline means she chose; fill means she was right). The result lands in the neutral problem slab — card ground, stone trim, big Jersey — on ease-out, never the pop curve. Tricks adds no sound at all.

Entry RULED: deck select is the door (a fourth row — book icon, no DUE chip, no tier bar), and Round cleared offers a targeted stone link when one table accounts for two or more misses ("×9 came up twice. Want the trick? ›"). Home is refused; the wrong-answer state is refused — nothing appears on a failure-adjacent state.
The picker is a push from deck select; trick pages push from the picker. No bar anywhere; the picker's bottom edge carries the contract line instead.

The stage is a SLOT (work order D). Array carries nine of the twelve; ×10 drafts the DIGITS stage (digit tiles in the paper language, the zero slides in) which ×11's "say the digit twice" will reuse; The Flip drafts the two-line SIMULTANEOUS ledger — both statements land on one frame, because a sequential reveal would imply the second derives from the first.
One deliberate frame deviation for Design to veto: The Flip has no chip strip — it is not a table, and 7 × 8 is its canonical case. Remaining pages to draw: 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12 — all reuse these stages.
